title: Grateful Dead Live at The Matrix on 1966-11-29

ai_review.summary: A historically rich but uneven 1966 show with rare early tracks; the soundboard tape is hollow and mis‑matched, yet the rarities shine through.
ai_review.review: The recording captures a noteworthy slice of Dead history – first Me & My Uncle, Mindbender, Lindy and other early‑era gems – but suffers from a thin, tin‑can sound, multi‑generation distortion and a mislabeled first set taken from another date. Performance quality is uneven: Jerry has flashes of brilliance while Bob’s vocals are weak, and several songs feel sloppy, though the rare numbers provide plenty of excitement for ’66 fans.

ai_rating.rationale: Show is historically interesting with several standout rarities (≈3.8/5) but the recording is thin, distorted and partially mis‑sourced (≈2.5/5); weighted average yields a mid‑range rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: First eight tracks are from 5/19/66, causing mis‑labeling; overall sound described as hollow, tin‑can like with distortion and multi‑generation artifacts; some cuts (Me & My Uncle, Viola Lee Blues) noted; despite age it is still listenable for fans.

standout_songs: One Kind Favor (See That My Grave Is Kept Clean)
"I Just Want to Make Love With You"
show_quality.setlist_flow: The tape mixes two different dates, confusing the set order; once the genuine 11/29 material is isolated it flows well with rare early numbers, but the mis‑matched first half disrupts continuity.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Shows spots of brilliance but also repeats licks and struggles on some songs (Same Thing, Viola Lee Blues).
band_member_comments.Bob: Vocals sound weak on this early recording; overall performance described as uneven.
